editorial:
Imagine a family where everyone is rich, mean, and obsessed with money. That is exactly what you get with the Van Doorns. The head of the house, Cornelis, runs a massive company that does two very different things: selling meat and making birth control. He is the boss of everything, but he is getting old and wants to retire. The problem is that his kids and relatives are a mess. They do not care about family values; they only care about who gets the keys to the kingdom and the big bank accounts. It feels like a soap opera but with more greed and a much darker tone.

You will notice that the acting is solid, and the way the family fights for power keeps you interested. It is not a fast movie, but it is rewarding if you like watching people be bad to each other. Some parts might feel a bit slow, but the drama makes up for it. If you can find it, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best quality, or you can try renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick if you love old-school family battles.
endingExplained: As the movie wraps up, you see that the fight for the company does not have a happy ending. Cornelis realizes that none of his heirs are actually fit to lead. The greed and lack of morals within the family eventually tear them apart. Instead of a smooth handoff of power, the business becomes a tool for conflict. The movie ends by showing that money cannot fix a broken family and that their lust for power only left them empty.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about wealthy families fighting over an inheritance.
